messages:
jamie: quick brain dump — thinking about moving most per-request RBAC checks out of the Console frontend and into the query layer (service-side). the goal is fewer roundtrips for complex dashboards + fewer backend calls from the browser. thoughts?

nina: curious — are you saying authz at query-time instead of pre-filtering in the UI? how would we keep latency under the console SLO (100ms for small dashboards)?

jamie: yes, exact. idea is: UI does a cheap coarse-grained check (feature flag + tenant in view), Query layer does authoritative RBAC per data-edge. benefits: single place to reason about policies, consistent answers across clients, avoids stale client caches. cons: more work in query path, potential tail latency impact.

mark: main worry is tail latency and cache invalidation. if we push checks to query layer we need a very fast policy cache (in-memory sharded) with TTL and watch invalidations. otherwise we add 10-50ms to many requests.

leila: can we do a hybrid? sample heavy dashboards and keep pre-filtering for “hot” views. also add a fallback fast-path: if policy cache miss, return a permissive placeholder with a background recheck?

jamie: hybrid is what i had in mind. propose "thresholded cache" model:

- short TTL policy cache (200-500ms) coalesced per tenant
- if cache hit -> enforce locally and return
- if miss -> do a quorum authz call to authz-service (fast path), but allow a low-cost optimistic response for non-critical widgets with a flag `soft_authz=true`

mark: ugh optimistic responses worry me. that could leak rows. need strict defaults. maybe optimistic-only for UI-only visualizations (counts) not raw row access.

nina: agree. also we should measure: p50/p95/p99 of authz check added to query. we might accept p50=+6ms p95=+20ms but p99 must be <100ms. that implies colocating cache with query worker.

jamie: implementation sketch:
```
- policy-cache service inside query-worker (L1) backed by central policy-store (L2)
- invalidations via policy-watch stream (kafka) and tombstones
- metric: policy_cache_hit_ratio, authz_call_latency_histogram
```

leila: for multi-tenant scaling, sharding cache by tenant-range + LRUs makes sense. For Dedicated customers we can pin heavy tenants to dedicated shards.

mark: also call out telemetry + explainability: query layer must emit why a row was filtered (policy-id, rule-id) for debugging + audits. add structured fields to traces.

jamie: yes — add trace/span tag `authz.policy=policy::<id>` and event when fallback occurred.

nina: ops question: rollout plan? we should behind a console feature flag + canary on 5% of requests, plus canary on dedicated tenants. add kill-switch at routing layer.

jamie: proposed rollout:
1) feature flag in console and query (opt-in)
2) internal canary on staging dashboards (two weeks)
3) 5% user traffic canary with detailed metrics and synthetic dashboards
4) ramp to 50% then global

leila: also add audit log retention knob. enterprise customers will want full decision logs (KMS/HSM ok).

mark: one more tradeoff — we must keep the console UI fast even when query authz is slower. plan for graceful degradation: show partial widgets with a spinner and a clear lock icon if authz fallback pending. UX will need copy. cc @design.

jamie: action items:
- mark: prototype policy-cache inside query-worker and measure p50/p95/p99 (due EOW)
- leila: sharding sketch + eviction strategy (due next Tue)
- nina: rollout plan doc + metrics list (due Wed)
- jamie: RFC followup with diagrams + sample JSON traces (due Fri)

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled for 1726512000 — will report status. :eyes:

nina: ok, good convo. small ask: include explicit guarantee matrix in RFC (what we guarantee if optimistic allowed vs strict).

jamie: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
